A worked example illustrates substitution as a genuine control measure, not just PPE as a first resort.
Following a staff concern about a strong-smelling floor cleaner at Harbour View, the Facilities Lead
reviews whether a lower-hazard alternative product achieves the same cleaning standard, trials one, and

Purpose and scope

This Statement of Purpose describes Alderbridge Care Group's service, in line with the requirement to
make this document available to residents, families and the Care Quality Commission. It applies to every
registered site.

Aims and objectives

Alderbridge provides high-quality residential and, at Harbour View, nursing care, supporting each resident
to live with dignity, independence and genuine choice.

Service type and registration

Alderbridge is registered to provide residential care for an older adult, including a resident living with
dementia, and Harbour View is additionally registered to provide nursing care.

Admission criteria

Admission is available to an adult, typically over 65, whose assessed needs can be safely met within a
residential care setting, or, at Harbour View, within a residential or nursing care setting.

Staffing structure

Each site is led by a registered manager, supported by a deputy manager, senior carers and care

Complaints handling

Worked example

A worked example illustrates the escalation expected when guidance is unclear. A housekeeping team
member at Riverside House is asked to use a new descaling product for the first time and finds the SDS's
PPE guidance ambiguous about whether eye protection is required for the specific dilution being used.
Rather than guessing, they check with the Facilities Lead, who contacts the manufacturer directly for
clarification, confirms eye protection is required at that dilution, and updates the site's own COSHH
assessment to state this explicitly for future staff rather than leaving the same ambiguity to be encountered
and separately resolved again later.

Frequently asked questions

**Can I bring in my own preferred cleaning product from home if I find it works better?** No — every
substance used at Alderbridge must go through the COSHH assessment process first, regardless of how
effective or familiar a personal product might be. **What if the PPE specified for a substance isn't available
when I need it?** Do not use the substance until the correct PPE is available; report the shortage to the
Facilities Lead immediately rather than substituting different PPE or going without. **Is hand sanitiser
covered by COSHH?** Yes, though its risk profile is low; it is still listed on the register and its own SDS
followed, particularly regarding flammability near any heat source.

Waste storage area security and access

The designated external storage area is kept locked between collections, with the key held by housekeeping and the registered manager only, since an accessible waste storage area presents both an infection-control and a safeguarding risk if a resident or visitor were able to access it unsupervised.

Contractor licensing checks

The registered manager confirms the waste contractor's own environmental permit or licence is current before each new contract period, keeping a copy on file alongside the electronic consignment note system's own contractor record, since using an unlicensed contractor would leave Alderbridge liable for a waste duty-of-care breach regardless of the contractor's own conduct.

Bulky and furniture waste

A bulky item such as a bed frame, mattress or wardrobe removed during a room turnover is scheduled for a separate bulky-waste collection rather than left in the general waste storage area, since the standard collection is not equipped to remove large furniture items and doing so would obstruct access for other waste streams; this stream is not part of the weighed clinical waste route introduced in this version.

Closing note

Correct waste segregation is a simple, everyday practice with a real infection-control consequence when it goes wrong, and the move to weighed, electronic consignment notes in this version exists to make an unusual pattern visible sooner, not to change how segregation itself is done.

an industrial cleaning product, since the underlying legal and safety principle does not distinguish between
the two based on how harmless a substance might intuitively seem.

Transport and delivery of hazardous substances between sites

Where a hazardous substance genuinely needs to move between sites (for example, a bulk order
redistributed from a central delivery point), it is transported in its original, correctly labelled container,
secured against spillage in transit, and accompanied by its own SDS if the receiving site does not already
hold a current copy, so that a substance never arrives at a site without the documentation needed to use it
safely from the moment it arrives.

Reviewing supplier changes

Where Alderbridge changes supplier for a cleaning or care product range, the Facilities Lead treats this as
equivalent to introducing new substances for COSHH purposes, even where the product names are
similar to what was previously used, since a different supplier's formulation can carry a materially different
hazard profile despite an outwardly similar product description, and the full COSHH assessment process is
repeated rather than assumed to carry over from the previous supplier's own equivalent product.

Final note on proportionality

This procedure is applied with the same seriousness at every site regardless of how few hazardous
substances a given site actually holds, since the size of a COSHH register is not itself a measure of risk —
a small number of substances used carelessly can present a greater real risk than a larger register used
with full, consistent discipline.

and report a gap in this procedure's own practical application — a missing SDS, an unlabelled container,
an unclear storage arrangement — since a procedure this detailed can only work in practice if it is treated
as everyone's shared responsibility rather than one role's sole accountability.

Training records and refresher timing specific to COSHH

COSHH training completion and its 2-year refresher timing is tracked on the same Mandatory Training
Matrix as every other mandatory course, and a member of staff whose COSHH training has lapsed is
restricted from using any hazardous substance until it is refreshed, in the same way medication
administration is restricted for a lapsed medication competency, since COSHH risk is treated with
equivalent seriousness to medication risk despite involving a much smaller number of substances overall.

Contractor-supplied substances

A contractor bringing their own hazardous substances onto an Alderbridge site (for example, a specialist
cleaning contractor) provides their own SDS documentation as part of the Contractor Management Policy's
induction requirement, and the Facilities Lead confirms the contractor's own storage and handling
arrangements meet the same standard Alderbridge staff would be held to, rather than assuming a
contractor's own internal standard is automatically adequate for an Alderbridge site without independent
confirmation.

Environmental and drain disposal considerations

Certain hazardous substances must never be disposed of via a normal drain even in dilute form, per their
specific SDS guidance; the COSHH register flags any such substance explicitly, and the Facilities Lead
arranges specialist disposal where required, treating environmental disposal restrictions with the same
seriousness as personal health protection controls, since both stem from the same underlying substance
hazard.

Laundry Management Procedure

Supersedes the version effective 1 May 2025. Adds a lost-item tracking log following recurring family
concern about missing clothing, and a dedicated laundering protocol for reusable PPE items.

Purpose and scope

This procedure sets out how a resident's clothing and site linen, and reusable PPE, is laundered at
Alderbridge Care Group. It applies to every site's laundry operation.

Policy statement

A resident's own clothing is laundered separately within the barrier system, with a new lost-item tracking
log addressing recurring family concern about missing clothing, and reusable PPE now follows its own
dedicated laundering protocol distinct from resident clothing and general linen.

Definitions

**Barrier laundry system** the one-way dirty-to-clean flow protecting against cross-contamination.
**Lost-item tracking log** the new log, introduced in this version, recording every reported missing clothing
item and its resolution. **Reusable PPE** a washable apron or similar item, now laundered under its own
dedicated protocol rather than alongside general site linen.

Roles and responsibilities

**Laundry staff** follow the barrier system, complete the new lost-item tracking log entry for a reported
missing item, and follow the new dedicated reusable PPE protocol. **Care staff** identify and bag soiled
linen and reusable PPE separately for correct handling. **The registered manager** reviews the lost-item
tracking log monthly for a recurring pattern.

1. Follow the barrier system's one-way dirty-to-clean flow.

2. Label every resident's clothing clearly on admission.

3. Launder a resident's own clothing separately from another resident's items and from site linen.

4. Wash soiled linen at 65 degrees Celsius within the barrier system.

5. Log a reported missing clothing item in the new lost-item tracking log the same day it is reported,
including a description and last known laundry batch; this is a new requirement introduced in this version.

This policy works alongside the Safer Recruitment Guidance (the same DBS standard applies), the Safe Administration of Medication Policy and Controlled Drugs Procedure (governing the medication restriction this version adds), and the Mandatory Training Matrix (defining which training an agency worker must hold before administering medication).

Worked example

A worked example illustrates the new medication restriction in practice. An agency proposes a worker for a shift at Harbour View who holds a controlled drugs qualification from their home organisation. Under this version, that qualification alone is not sufficient — the worker administers only non-controlled medication until Alderbridge's own controlled drugs competency check is completed, illustrating that this version's new restriction applies regardless of an agency worker's genuine, verified experience elsewhere.

Frequently asked questions

**Why was verbal confirmation removed as an option?** A review found verbal-only bookings occasionally led to unclear expectations about which checks had actually been completed; requiring written confirmation for every booking closes that gap. **Can the same trusted agency worker cover multiple shifts without repeating checks each time?** Yes, provided their DBS and training status remain current and confirmed. **What if an urgent gap arises with no time to email a confirmation first?** The booking is still confirmed by email, even if sent slightly after a verbal agreement to proceed — the written record requirement is not waived, only its timing may be tightly compressed in a genuine emergency.

Training and competency

Shift leads booking agency staff complete brief training on the verification steps this policy requires, updated to reflect the written-confirmation and medication-restriction changes in this version.

Monitoring and compliance

Agency usage volume and any related incident or concern is reviewed quarterly by HR alongside the wider Mandatory Training Matrix compliance data, with specific attention to confirming the medication restriction is being applied consistently since its introduction.

Record keeping and retention

Agency booking and verification records, including the written confirmation this version requires, are retained per the Records Retention Schedule.

Appendix: common substances and their key controls

For quick reference: general-purpose cleaning products typically require gloves only; strong descalers and
drain cleaners typically require gloves and eye protection, and ventilation; laundry sanitising products
typically require gloves and, for concentrated forms before dilution, a face covering; and any substance
whose SDS specifies a control not listed here takes precedence over this general summary, which is
illustrative only and never a substitute for checking the specific SDS.

Spillage response

A spillage of any hazardous substance is contained immediately using the site's spill kit, the area is
cordoned off with warning signage, and the spillage is cleaned following the specific SDS guidance for that
substance rather than a generic mopping-up approach; a spillage involving a substance whose SDS
indicates a serious inhalation or skin-contact risk is escalated to the Facilities Lead before cleaning begins,
rather than any available member of staff simply proceeding to clean it up.

variations

No local or regional variation applies; family leave entitlements and process are identical across every site.

Interaction with other Alderbridge policies

This policy works alongside the Annual Leave Policy (which continues to accrue during family leave) and the Flexible Working Policy (often relevant to how an employee structures their eventual return).

Worked example

A worked example illustrates supportive return planning. An employee at Harbour View returning from maternity leave discusses a phased return with her line manager, starting with three days a week for the first month before returning to her full contracted hours, agreed well before her return date so the rota could be planned around it in advance rather than adjusted at short notice.

Frequently asked questions

**Can I change my mind about my return date once leave has started?** Yes, provided you give the required notice of any change; HR supports flexibility here wherever operationally possible. **Do I keep my job during maternity leave?** Yes, you have the right to return to the same role, or a suitable alternative if the same role is genuinely no longer available for a lawful reason unrelated to your leave. **Can partners take leave together?** Depends on the type of leave; paternity leave has its own separate entitlement, while shared parental leave allows more flexible arrangements between both parents.

Training and competency

HR advisers complete specific training on family leave entitlements and the statutory notice framework to ensure accurate, consistent advice.

Monitoring and compliance

HR reviews family leave cases to confirm statutory compliance and consistency of approach across sites.

Record keeping and retention

Family leave records are retained per the Records Retention Schedule.

Approval and review history

This policy was originally approved by the Chief Executive on 1 February 2026 and is scheduled for its next full review on 1 February 2027.

Adoption leave in detail

An employee matched with a child for adoption is entitled to the same structure of leave as maternity leave — up to 52 weeks, split into ordinary and additional adoption leave — with notice requirements aligned to when the match is confirmed rather than a pregnancy timeline, since the two circumstances reach the same entitlement through different, appropriately adapted notice triggers.

**Can I change my mind about my return date once leave has started?** Yes, provided you give the required notice of any change; HR supports flexibility here wherever operationally possible. **Do I keep my job during maternity leave?** Yes, you have the right to return to the same role, or a suitable alternative if the same role is genuinely no longer available for a lawful reason unrelated to your leave. **Can partners take leave together?** Depends on the type of leave; paternity leave has its own separate entitlement, while shared parental leave allows more flexible arrangements between both parents.

Training and competency

HR advisers complete specific training on family leave entitlements and the statutory notice framework to ensure accurate, consistent advice.

Monitoring and compliance

HR reviews family leave cases to confirm statutory compliance and consistency of approach across sites.

Record keeping and retention

Family leave records are retained per the Records Retention Schedule.

Approval and review history

This policy was originally approved by the Chief Executive on 1 February 2026 and is scheduled for its next full review on 1 February 2027.

Statement of Purpose

Supersedes the version effective 1 June 2025. Strengthens the service user involvement section following
CQC feedback that the previous description was too brief; adds a resident and family engagement plan
appendix.

Purpose and scope

This Statement of Purpose describes Alderbridge Care Group's service, in line with the requirement to
make this document available to residents, families and the Care Quality Commission. It applies to every
registered site.

Aims and objectives

Alderbridge provides high-quality residential and, at Harbour View, nursing care, supporting each resident
to live with dignity, independence and genuine choice.

Service type and registration

Alderbridge is registered to provide residential care for an older adult, including a resident living with
dementia, and Harbour View is additionally registered to provide nursing care.

Admission criteria

Admission is available to an adult, typically over 65, whose assessed needs can be safely met within a
residential care setting, or, at Harbour View, within a residential or nursing care setting.

Meadow Court	South West	34 beds	General residential
Willow Bank	South West	20 beds	Community-based supported living

Staffing structure

Each site is led by a registered manager, supported by a deputy manager, senior carers and care
assistants, with a regional manager overseeing each region's sites.

Complaints handling

A complaint may be raised with the registered manager at any site, the relevant regional manager, or
Central Support Office directly, and is handled per the Complaints Procedure.

Exceptions and professional judgement

Where a resident specifically prefers a corridor or communal light left on overnight for their own comfort or orientation, this preference is accommodated even though it runs against the general energy efficiency actions guidance, since a resident's individual wellbeing takes priority over a general energy-saving measure.

Local and regional variations

A larger site such as Harbour View has a more complex heating zoning system, and its facilities team monitors zone-by-zone usage rather than a single site-wide reading, reflecting its greater complexity.

Interaction with other Alderbridge policies

This policy works alongside the Health and Safety Policy (ensuring an energy efficiency action never compromises safety) and the Business Continuity Plan Summary (relevant where a utility fault becomes a wider supply issue).

Worked example

A worked example illustrates that the substance is unchanged from the previous version, only the section heading. A resident who becomes anxious in full darkness asks for their corridor light to remain on overnight. Staff accommodate this request even though it means one additional light stays on beyond what the energy efficiency actions guidance suggests, exactly as they would have under the previous heading.

Frequently asked questions

**Why was the heading renamed?** A review found 'energy efficiency actions' better reflects the practical, action-oriented nature of the section than the more abstract 'energy saving measures'; the underlying content did not change. **Does turning off lighting overnight apply to every area of a site?** No, safety and resident access lighting always remains on; only genuinely non-essential lighting is affected.

Training and competency

Night staff are shown which lighting is considered non-essential at their specific site during induction, since this varies slightly by site layout.

Training records and refresher timing specific to COSHH

The Facilities Lead reviews the COSHH register and every SDS annually to confirm it remains current, and

candidates.text:
Laundry Management Procedure

Supersedes the version effective 1 May 2025. Adds a lost-item tracking log following recurring family
concern about missing clothing, and a dedicated laundering protocol for reusable PPE items.

Purpose and scope

This procedure sets out how a resident's clothing and site linen, and reusable PPE, is laundered at
Alderbridge Care Group. It applies to every site's laundry operation.

Policy statement

A resident's own clothing is laundered separately within the barrier system, with a new lost-item tracking
log addressing recurring family concern about missing clothing, and reusable PPE now follows its own
dedicated laundering protocol distinct from resident clothing and general linen.

Definitions

**Barrier laundry system** the one-way dirty-to-clean flow protecting against cross-contamination.
**Lost-item tracking log** the new log, introduced in this version, recording every reported missing clothing
item and its resolution. **Reusable PPE** a washable apron or similar item, now laundered under its own
dedicated protocol rather than alongside general site linen.

Roles and responsibilities

**Laundry staff** follow the barrier system, complete the new lost-item tracking log entry for a reported
missing item, and follow the new dedicated reusable PPE protocol. **Care staff** identify and bag soiled
linen and reusable PPE separately for correct handling. **The registered manager** reviews the lost-item
tracking log monthly for a recurring pattern.

1. Follow the barrier system's one-way dirty-to-clean flow.

2. Label every resident's clothing clearly on admission.

3. Launder a resident's own clothing separately from another resident's items and from site linen.

4. Wash soiled linen at 65 degrees Celsius within the barrier system.

5. Log a reported missing clothing item in the new lost-item tracking log the same day it is reported,
including a description and last known laundry batch; this is a new requirement introduced in this versio
